title: Strict log-concavity in the first type-B q-Stirling column
summary: In the first column of the second-kind array, strict log-concavity begins at row six.
verification: The classification was formally checked in Lean.

title: A 19-vertex counterexample to Graffiti.pc 138
summary: A tree whose longest path has 17 vertices, one fewer than the conjecture requires.
verification: Direct proof and an exhaustive check of the 19-vertex tree.

title: Graffiti.pc 392b on 2-domination and matchings
summary: A matching bound on the number of vertices needed to give every unmarked vertex two marked neighbors.
verification: The full theorem was formally checked in Lean.

title: One-sided log-concavity for a column of the type B q-Stirling numbers
summary: Proves the parity inequality on the rising side of first-kind column one at every rank, and on the second diagonal of both families. The unrestricted conjecture remains open.
verification: The formal proof was checked in Lean.

title: Coefficient inequalities for the type B q-Stirling numbers
summary: A combined technical note on seven Lean-verified results. Strict adjacent log-concavity in second-kind column one begins at rank six for ranks at least two. The note also proves a rising-side inequality in first-kind column one and parity log-concavity on the second diagonal of both families.
verification: The formal proof was checked in Lean.

title: Two partial results on the Seacrest–Seacrest graph-grabbing conjecture
summary: On even connected bipartite graphs with no induced once-subdivided claw, Alice can secure half the weight if adjacent positive weights agree. A second result compares opposite choices of the last vertex on a path with attached leaves. The general conjecture remains open.
verification: The formal proof was checked in Lean.

title: A counterexample to Songsuwan’s period-two conjecture for Node-Kayles
summary: On a fixed 291-vertex graph, attach copies of the same five-vertex path at one vertex. The Node-Kayles values are 8 and 9 at arbitrarily large branch counts two apart. This disproves Songsuwan’s Conjecture 2.
verification: The formal proof was checked in Lean.
